newsitem.title: USA: Clinton orders rules making gun sales harder.
newsitem.headline: Clinton orders rules making gun sales harder.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday signed an order tightening restrictions on gun-buyers, including foreigners, saying firearms have been reaching "the wrong hands" with tragic results.
The directive stems from last month's shooting at the Empire State Building in New York, in which a Palestinian visitor killed one person was and wounded six before committing suicide.
In signing it, Clinton said the new regulation "will make it harder for people to come to America, purchase weapons and commit crimes against Americans."

The gunman in the New York skyscraper shooting, identified as Ali Abu Kamal, came to the United States in December and bought his semiautomatic handgun in Florida after staying in a motel there for three weeks. He attacked sight-seers on an observation deck.

Clinton also ordered all federal law enforcement agencies to require their personnel to place child safety locks on their weapons, and he renewed a request for legislation banning so-called "cop-killer", or armour-piercing, bullets.

In an Oval Office ceremony, Clinton said he was announcing "a series of new steps we must take immediately to protect our children, our neighbours and our police officers from tragedies caused by firearms in the wrong hands."
"We were all shocked to learn of the foreign gunman who shot seven people on top of the Empire State Building, killing one of them, and then killing himself," the president said.

"He apparently bought this gun after living in a Florida motel for just three weeks," Clinton said, complaining that the current application to buy a weapon "does not even ask how long an applicant has lived at his or her current address."

Under the order, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, which enforces gun-control laws, will immediately require applicants to certify they have been residents for at least 90 days in the state where they want to buy a gun.
The National Rifle Association condemned Clinton's actions and accused him of tring to divert attention from legal and ethical woes surrounding Democratic fundraising.
"The Clinton proposals mean no hunting, no self-defence and no safety," said Tanya Metaksa, executive director of the NRA's Institute for Legislative Action.
Metaksa called the the actions "desperation tactics by a president embroiled in ethical ... scandals," adding, "Clinton's proposal clearly undermines armed self-defence in American homes."
Citing the soaring death rate of children killed by firearms in the United States, Clinton warned that "easy access means deadly consequences."
"Guns cause one in every four deaths of teenagers aged 15 to 19," he said in calling upon Congress to enact legislation that requires child-proof safety locks on firearms.
"America cannot tolerate this. Congress should pass my proposal to require these locks with every hand gun in the very near future."
He also chided Congress for failing to pass legislation that would outlaw "cop killer" bullets that puncture bullet-proof vests.
"I have sent this legislation to Congress twice before and they failed to act," he said. "They should not delay this effort again."

"If a bullet can tear through a bulletproof vest like a hot knife through butter, it should be against the law, and that is the bottom line," Clinton said. "These bullets are designed for one purpose only, to kill police officers."
